steps.what: Review relevant current service assignments and case context in the clinical case system in {OTHER}.
Supervise or direct workers providing services, observing practice and addressing actual client needs.
Evaluate worker understanding and service safety, correcting guidance and unresolved responsibilities.

outputs: Human judgement of service readiness and further supervision needs

tasks.design: Configure a permission-limited current-assignment view in the clinical case-system category of {OTHER}. It reduces repeated tab navigation before supervision; the counselor still reads the actual context, directs staff and checks understanding without automated allocation or performance scoring.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant existing assignments and context may sit on separate screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved views can consolidate navigation without interpreting worker performance.
tasks.still_hard: Safe delegation and recognising when a worker needs direct support depend on context.
tasks.human_edge: Understand a worker's uncertainty and intervene before service quality suffers.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less screen navigation; supervision and decision rights remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native permission-limited views can reduce navigation to existing case context without replacing supervision.

assumptions: Boundary is actual supervision, not a new staffing roster, supervision report or performance-monitoring programme. No trailing record is assumed where the live guidance is the actual output. Any separately required case changes remain their actual clinical workflow, with no claimed saving here.

Existing treating staff produce assignment id, responsible worker, case id and current service status in ordinary care records. Their normal record work is unchanged and gets no benefit. S1 counts reading and resolving missing/stale context; no new structured capture is required by this design.

tasks.short: Modify treatment plans when client status changes

steps.what: Review actual changed client status and the current treatment plan in the clinical system in {OTHER}.
inputs: Actual status changes and clinical evidence

steps.what: Discuss changed needs, preferences and practical constraints with the client and relevant care contacts.
Decide how treatment goals, interventions and review timing must change for the client.
Write modified treatment plan details in the existing clinical plan form in {OTHER}.
Check modified plan wording, dates and consistency against actual decisions and changed status.
inputs: Actual status changes and clinical evidence

steps.what: Save the ordinary authored treatment plan update in the clinical record.

tasks.design: Configure the existing treatment-plan form in the clinical case-system category of {OTHER} to reuse verified case headers and unchanged section structure. The counselor decides and writes every substantive change and checks the finished plan; no model selects treatment and no automatic order or message is issued.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rewriting fixed case headings is mixed with the clinically important modification.
tasks.enabler_now: Native plan forms can retain stable identifiers and headings without copying obsolete treatment instructions.
tasks.still_hard: A changed status can require reassessing risk, trust and the feasibility of interventions.
tasks.human_edge: Agree a realistic change with the client and take responsibility for its clinical meaning.
tasks.altitude: Small documentation saving; clinical judgement and responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Native plan forms can reuse stable case headers while substantive treatment changes remain authored by a counselor.

assumptions: Boundary is modifying the client's authored care-plan record, not prescribing, referral, automatic activation of an intervention or external release. Any distinct order or send requires its own actual workflow; none is claimed here.

Current clinical records contain case id, client id, plan id and section labels, produced by ordinary intake and prior care. S1 verifies the current case and status; s2 captures new needs and s3 makes the decisions. S4 manually writes changed goals, interventions and dates; no structured decision feed or automatic clinical prose is assumed.

Test native form reuse first. S4's15% cut removes3 provisional hours of repeating stable case identifiers and structural headings, leaving17 for actual changed content and correction. Old goals are not silently carried forward. S5 is the ordinary factual check, not a new self-approval stage; s6 is fully retained and ungated.
unknowns: Actual fixed header repetition within plan writing
research_questions: Can stable identifiers be reused without preselecting an obsolete goal, risk judgement or review date?

tasks.short: Instruct staff in program methods and procedures

steps.what: Find and read the current program methods and procedures in {DOCS} for instruction.
Instruct others in program methods, procedures and functions, demonstrating practical application.
Check staff understanding through actual practice and correct unsafe or mistaken interpretations.
outputs: Human assessment of understanding and further instruction needs

tasks.design: Configure a direct current-procedure index in {DOCS} so the counselor can reach the approved source without repeated folder searches. Instruction, demonstration and checking of practical understanding remain human; the index generates no treatment advice or certification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current version can interrupt otherwise human instruction.
tasks.enabler_now: Native version links and topic indexing can remove source navigation without writing new training material.
tasks.still_hard: Staff may repeat a procedure correctly but misunderstand when its use is inappropriate.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt an explanation to the learner and observe whether it changes safe practice.
tasks.altitude: No new decision rights; slightly less source searching before practical instruction.

evidence.claim: A current-version document index can reduce source navigation without replacing live instruction or competence assessment.

assumptions: Boundary is actual staff instruction, including genuine source lookup. It does not assume a slide deck is written for every interaction, a new course enrolment process or a completion record nobody maintains today.

The program owner produces approved procedure id, title, version, effective date and document link during existing procedure maintenance. No new source authoring is assumed free or moved to this task. S1 counts reading and verifying currentness; broken links and missing procedures return to manual lookup within retained work.

Test native current-version links first. The20% reduction on s1 removes3 provisional hours of repeated searching; all12 source-reading hours and all85 live instruction/practice hours remain. Existing direct access earns no saving.

tasks.design: Use the existing secure handoff form in the clinical case-system category of {OTHER} to reuse only case identifiers and fixed communication headings. evidence.claim: Native secure handoff forms can reuse fixed identifiers while people retain clinical wording, disclosure and recipient checks.

assumptions: Boundary is the actual liaison path requiring a written secure handoff to medical staff in the same care organisation. For an entirely oral liaison, do not add this message or its saving. Medical staff's clinical work is unchanged and no response-time benefit is claimed.
